name: bolognese
instructions:
BOLOGNESE — split back out of [[italian-tomato-sauce]] into its own file 2026-11-18 (variant A there since the 2026-11-13 merge; its own file before that).

Marcella Hazan's meat ragu — the canonical bolognese. 'MY BOLOGNESE' IS NO LONGER A SEPARATE BUILD (collapsed 2026-11-18, formerly A1/A2): it lives on as FOOTNOTES below — how to make it vegetarian, my adjustments, and comparison notes on ATK's and Nisha's recipes.

LENTILS, MUSHROOMS, AND WALNUTS ARE SECONDARY/OK in this recipe (see notes — the allowance does NOT extend to [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]]). The protein slot is a meat thing, real or fake — but IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF IS BANNED (clashing — it ages horribly; see notes). ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is the best fake.

The load-bearing recipe in this family. Marcella Hazan, Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking. If 'bolognese' means one thing in this cookbook, it's this one.

INGREDIENTS:
- vegetable oil + butter (the fat)
- yellow onions, celery, carrots — finely diced soffrito
- ground beef (or abbots ground beef as the substitute)
- milk
- nutmeg
- WHITE wine (Marcella's canonical; red wine also appears in some bolognese traditions — see WINE note)
- canned tomatoes
- black pepper
- pasta (traditionally tagliatelle, not spaghetti)
- parmesan cheese for serving

TECHNIQUE — MARCELLA'S NON-NEGOTIABLES:
1. Cook the beef ONLY until it loses raw color. Do NOT brown it. Browning gives a different (and lesser) ragu.
2. Milk goes in BEFORE wine. The milk coats the meat and protects it from the wine acid; reversing the order changes the texture.
3. Bare-simmer for THREE+ HOURS uncovered. Splash in water if it dries out. The long uncovered simmer is what makes it a bolognese; cutting time turns it into a generic meat sauce.
4. Fat should separate at the end. That's the visual signal you're done.

=== FOOTNOTES (THE OLD 'MY BOLOGNESE', COLLAPSED 2026-11-18) ===

VEGETARIAN: some kind of VEGAN BEEF is the BARE MINIMUM — the meat-thing-minimum rule; it's like a french beef stew, you need a meat thing even if it's fake. ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is best; IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND IS BANNED (ages horribly — see notes). Add PORCINI POWDER + NUTRITIONAL YEAST for the glutamates the real meat would bring — A LOT of porcini powder makes a difference.

MY ADJUSTMENTS: NO CARROTS (too sweet — celery/onion soffrito) + GARLIC; THYME + OREGANO (rosemary when there's actual meat); CANNED TOMATO SAUCE (half a can) with ENOUGH MILK THAT IT'S CREAMY, instead of paste or crushed; DARK BALSAMIC VINEGAR finish (Nisha's discovery — incomplete without it); TOASTED WALNUTS optional (don't overdo — they can embitter, and watch the nutmeg too); GRUYERE over parmesan at the end; serve with a PASTA WATER EMULSION.

COMPARISONS: see the Nisha footnote in notes (where she's wrong and right) and the ATK note (their mushroom bolognese — git history only).
notes:
=== SPLIT BACK OUT 2026-11-18 ===

Merged into [[italian-tomato-sauce]] 2026-11-13 as variant A; split back into its own file 2026-11-18 (near-verbatim). The protein-free sauces (gnocchi, vodka, porcini) remain in that house; [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]] split out in the same pass.

=== TOMATO RULING — ALL ITALIAN TOMATO SAUCES (2026-11-18) ===

FRESH TOMATOES ARE TOO RAW AND SOUR — they don't give enough umami on their own. CANNED CHUNKY TOMATOES WITH TOMATO PASTE, or CANNED TOMATO SAUCE, are ideal. FIRE-ROASTED canned tomatoes aren't right either — they have a better flavor profile for MEXICAN and INDIAN food. (Shared ruling with [[italian-tomato-sauce]] and [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]].)

=== TOMATO FORMS IN THIS FILE ===

CANNED WHOLE TOMATOES are the base. CRUSHED TOMATOES and TOMATO PASTE are CLASHING in this dish (from the old house rulings); the my-adjustments path uses CANNED TOMATO SAUCE (half a can, creamy with milk) instead. PARSLEY clashing (see the herb note). CREAM clashing — MILK is the dairy.

THE BOLOGNESE SHAPE:
1. A tomato base (canned tomatoes + often tomato paste; regular canned only — no fire-roasted; that was [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]]' old smoky direction until the 2026-11-18 tomato ruling removed it).
2. A protein slot: a MEAT THING — real ground beef (Marcella), or vegan beef at bare minimum when vegetarian (ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is best — impossible/beyond is banned; see the vegetarian footnote). Lentils and mushrooms are secondary/OK (see below).
3. An acid: wine (white per Marcella's canonical; red per Nisha) + the balsamic finish in my adjustments. See WINE note.
4. Soffrito-style FINELY DICED aromatics: yellow onion always in; celery/garlic; carrots per Marcella (out in my adjustments).
5. Long simmer intent (3+ hours).
6. Dairy: milk in both.
7. Served over pasta.

=== WINE — WHITE AND RED BOTH APPEAR ===

Both white and red wine appear frequently across canonical bolognese recipes:
- MARCELLA: WHITE wine, canonically. Milk goes in first as a protective coat; white wine follows.
- NISHA: RED wine per her tradition; either works.
- CROSS-USE: either wine can work if that's what you have. Sticking to canonical is safer, but the family absorbs either.

Both wines are primary ingredients in this file for that reason.

=== FOOTNOTE — HOW TO MAKE IT VEGETARIAN (THE MEAT-THING-MINIMUM RULE: VEGAN BEEF IS THE FLOOR; ABBOTS IS BEST; IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND IS BANNED) ===

Core rule for the vegetarian path: some kind of VEGAN BEEF is the BARE MINIMUM. It's like a FRENCH BEEF STEW — you need a meat thing, even if it's fake. The old vegetarian protein path (lentils + walnuts) no longer defines the core recipe. ABBOTS GROUND BEEF is the best fake-meat pick — same verdict as [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]].

IMPOSSIBLE/BEYOND BEEF — BANISHED AGAIN (CLASHING): it tastes good for 30 MINUTES after you make it, but it tastes HORRIBLE THE DAY AFTER — it becomes a GUMMY, CANDY-LIKE thing: not even sweet, just VERY ARTIFICIAL tasting. REMOVING CARROTS ISN'T ENOUGH. (This reverses the earlier reprieve — the carrots-out + balsamic/milk logic addressed the too-sweet problem, but the day-after aging failure is its own thing and it's disqualifying.)

=== FOOTNOTE (MY ADJUSTMENT) — CARROTS OUT, TOO SWEET ===

When I make it, carrots are out: TOO SWEET. The soffrito is celery + onion. Marcella's canonical soffrito keeps them.

=== LENTILS, MUSHROOMS, AND WALNUTS — SECONDARY/OK ===

Lentils, mushrooms, and walnuts are SECONDARY — OK in this recipe (walked forward from 'out entirely but orthogonal'). The allowance is bolognese-specific: they are NOT OK in [[french-beef-and-mushroom-stew]].

THERE IS NO MUSHROOM-FORWARD PASTA IN THE COOKBOOK ANYMORE — the mushroom alfredo idea was removed 2026-11-13 (mushrooms are better in antipasti: [[mushroom-antipasto]]). (2026-11-17: the supermarket porcini sauce (marcella-inspired) joined [[italian-tomato-sauce]]. It's a tomato sauce with porcini rather than a mushroom-forward pasta, but the slot is no longer strictly empty.) Boscaiola — the rich cream + tomato paste + brandy expression — was retired 2026-11-13 (overly complicated); pasta al funghi, the lean expression, was deleted 2026-11-06. Lentil ragu history lives in the CONTEXT notes below.

=== FOOTNOTE (MY ADJUSTMENT) — HERBS: THYME + OREGANO; THE NO-HERB RULE OVERTURNED ===

THYME + OREGANO in my adjusted version (both were previously marked clashing — reversed). ROSEMARY goes well here WHEN THERE'S ACTUAL MEAT in it.

Marcella's canonical stays herb-free — the long simmer + milk-and-nutmeg register is its own thing, and fresh herb finishes don't take.

Parsley stays clashing: a porcini powder/mushroom/parsley braise (Marcella — now [[mushroom-antipasto]]) would be good AS A SIDE to this — parsley doesn't need integration into the sauce itself.

=== FOOTNOTE — PORCINI + NOOCH IF VEGETARIAN ===

When made vegetarian (abbots/vegan beef), the recipe benefits from PORCINI MUSHROOM POWDER + NUTRITIONAL YEAST — glutamate support for what the real meat would otherwise bring. Following [[pub-style-lentils]] rules (porcini powder adds glutamates without tipping the scales), A LOT of porcini powder makes a difference here. (Whole mushrooms are secondary now — see the lentils/mushrooms/walnuts note.)

=== FOOTNOTE — THE NISHA COMPARISON ===

WHERE NISHA IS WRONG, AND WHERE SHE'S RIGHT: her tomato-paste-forward sauce is the miss — this dish wants CANNED TOMATO SAUCE (half a can) with enough milk to read CREAMY, not a paste-dark reduction. But she knocks it out of the park with the BALSAMIC VINEGAR — the dish is incomplete without it. MILK AND BALSAMIC BOTH STAY — confirmed on the latest rework.

MILK, NOT CREAM: heavy cream would be clashing here — MILK is the most appropriate dairy. (Marcella's call stands across both variants: milk's lighter body protects and loosens without tipping the sauce into a cream-sauce register.)

BITTERNESS WATCH — WALNUTS AND NUTMEG: both can embitter. Toasted-but-not-overdone walnuts (secondary now), and a measured hand on the nutmeg.

CHEESE IN THE POT: funky GRUYERE preferred over parmesan, melted in at the end (matches the grating preference for the canonical build).

=== DISTINCTION FROM FIRE-ROASTED-MEATBALLS ===

Split off from this file. That dish uses fire-roasted tomatoes (load-bearing) and the meatball shape (load-bearing). Neither belongs in bolognese-shape.

=== DISTINCTION FROM LENTIL-MUSHROOM-STEW ===

That dish is a stew, not a ragu — broth-forward, served as a soup, explicitly anti-canned-tomato and anti-tomato-paste, uses stock not pasta. The lentils that used to live in this file's vegetarian variant point there and to [[french-lentils]] now.

=== WHY BOLOGNESE GETS THE HEADLINE ===

This is the canonical italian ragu — Marcella Hazan's recipe is the cookbook's reference point. The three non-negotiables (don't brown the beef, milk before wine, three-hour uncovered simmer) define what 'bolognese' means here. The old 'my bolognese' build borrowed the shape without trying to be a copy of Marcella — collapsed into footnotes 2026-11-18.

NO FIRE-ROASTED TOMATOES IN THIS FILE: regular canned tomatoes only. (Fire-roasted was the signature of [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]] until 2026-11-18 — now out per the tomato ruling.)

TAGLIATELLE OVER SPAGHETTI: Marcella was explicit that bolognese is for tagliatelle, not spaghetti. The wide flat noodle holds the meat sauce; spaghetti slides under it. (My adjusted version is more forgiving — long-cut still preferred but ridged tubes (rigatoni, penne rigate) work fine.)

GRUYERE OVER PARMESAN FOR GRATING ON TOP — MY PREFERENCE: I prefer grated gruyere over grated parmesan as the finishing cheese. The funkiness agrees with the sauce.

=== CONTEXT — NISHA VORA'S LENTIL BOLOGNESE (REFERENCE) ===

Nisha Vora, Rainbow Plant Life — the recipe the old vegetarian variant grew out of. Her build: onions browned with water-deglazing, garlic + oregano + thyme, a whole TUBE of tomato paste caramelized dark, red wine deglaze, 3 cups vegetable broth, 1 cup soaked RED lentils + 1/4 cup toasted crushed walnuts, canned crushed tomatoes, ~35-40 min simmer, 1 tbsp aged balsamic finish, parsley garnish. Her load-bearing claims, kept for reference: TUBE tomato paste over canned (canned reads tinny); soak the red lentils 30-60 min; TOAST the walnuts (raw walnut doesn't deliver — same as the retired lentil wellington's lesson); quality balsamic or skip (cheap balsamic is watery sourness); a commenter found it acidic without dairy — which the milk-and-tomato-sauce rework addresses directly.

=== HISTORICAL NOTE — THE LENTIL/WALNUT AND MUSHROOM VARIANTS REMOVED ===

This file has walked through: four variants (Marcella; my mix; ATK mushroom; mushroom+lentil), then two (Marcella; lentil+walnut vegetarian), now two again with the vegetarian protein path replaced by the meat-thing-minimum rule. Mushrooms read stew; lentils now read as their own dish family. Both were orthogonal to bolognese for a while, then walked forward to secondary/OK (2026-11-04) — the same pass that banished impossible/beyond for its day-after aging failure.

ATK: their mushroom bolognese was one of the old four variants — its text survives only in git history; the comparison slot here is open if it's ever worth recovering.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- boscaiola (retired 2026-11-13, overly complicated): was the mushroom-forward pasta home (pasta al funghi, the lean sibling, deleted earlier). The mushroom-pasta slot is now empty — the mushroom alfredo idea was removed 2026-11-13 (mushrooms are better in antipasti). ([[italian-tomato-sauce]]'s supermarket porcini sauce, added 2026-11-17, is the nearest thing now.)
- [[spaghetti-and-meatballs]]: crushed tomatoes + meatball shape (fire-roasted removed 2026-11-18). Different shape.
- [[italian-tomato-sauce]] — the protein-free sauce house (gnocchi, vodka, porcini). This bolognese is the protein-forward, long-simmered counterpart.
